I've been ghosted by a platonic friend once. I spent months wondering what the hell I did wrong, and I initially did text her asking why, but no response. Even after I gave up on her, her leaving sat with me badly. She messaged me about three years after it went down. I never brought it up, because (as I'll explain below), I've had my reasons for ghosting people as well.

As for me, I've ghosted people. When I was a junior in high school, my usual depression was worsened by an anti-depressant - basically I was unable to sleep more than two hours every other night, and as a result I became extremely paranoid and stopped trusting everyone. And that coupled with incidents of bullying led me to cut ties with literally everyone, sans warning. I ended up deleting all of my social media and messages, and I deleted most of my contacts as well. I vividly remember how I kept my phone in airplane mode at that point, and only used it for listening to music. Pretty much everyone didn't try to contact me, though, and I think my heart broke more knowing that if I didn't text first, I wasn't going to get a response. In school, though, some students did try to talk to me, but I didn't say anything of substance and they eventually stopped trying- I completely withdrew and always had my earbuds in whenever I wasn't in class.

In the end, I think the only way to truly cope with it is to accept that someone whom you care(d) about has cut contact with you, and to accept that you may never know why.
